stem: The mathematical form of the first law of thermodynamics when heat (q) is supplied and W is work done by the system is: (a) ΔU=q+W (b) ΔU=q-W (c) ΔU=-q+W (d) ΔU=-q-W
An ideal gas undergoing expansion in vacuum shows: (a) ΔU = 0 (b) W = 0 (c) q = 0 (d) all of these
A system is provided 50 joule of heat and work done on the system is 10 J. The change in internal energy during the process is: (a) 40 J (b) 60 J (c) 80 J (d) 50 J
One mole of a gas occupying 3 dm³ expands against a constant external pressure of 1 atm to a volume of 13 dm³. The work done is: (a) -10 atm dm³ (b) -20 atm dm³ (c) -39 atm dm³ (d) -48 atm dm³

A gas expands against a variable pressure given by P = 20/V (where P is in atm and V is in L). During expansion from a volume of 1 litre to 10 litre, the gas undergoes a change in internal energy of 400 J. How much heat is absorbed by the gas during expansion? (a) 46 J (b) 4660 J (c) 5065.8 J (d) 4260 J
Derive an expression for pressure-volume (PV) work. OR Derive the expression for work when a gas expands against constant external pressure. OR Derive the equation: W = -P ex ΔV.
Explain sign convention of work during expansion and compression. OR Explain +W and -W.
Explain the work obtained in vacuum or free expansion. OR Comment on the statement: No work is involved in an expansion of a gas in vacuum.
One mole of an ideal gas is compressed from 500 cm³ against a constant external pressure of 1.2×10 5 Pa. The work involved in the process is 36.0 J. Calculate the final volume.
What is the work done in a free expansion of a gas? (a) Maximum (b) Infinite (c) Zero (d) Depends on temperature
Which of the following is the correct sign convention for work done by the system? (a) Positive (b) Negative (c) Zero (d) Infinite
What is the SI unit of heat? (a) Calorie (b) Newton (c) Joule (d) Watt
What is the value of 1 calorie in joules? (a) 1 J (b) 4.184 J (c) 0.239 J (d) 101.3 J
When a gas expands against an external pressure, the work is: (a) Zero (b) Positive (c) Negative (d) Maximum
Calculate the work done when a gas expands from 1 m³ to 2 m³ under a constant pressure of 100 kPa. (a) 100 kJ (b) 200 kJ (c) 150 kJ (d) 250 kJ
Convert 300 calories to joules. (a) 1252 J (b) 1125 J (c) 1255 J (d) 1400 J
A system does 50 J of work and absorbs 150 J of heat. Find the change in internal energy. (a) 100 J (b) 200 J (c) 150 J (d) 50 J
Convert 1 litre-atm of energy to joules. (a) 100 J (b) 4.184 J (c) 101.3 J (d) 0.239 J
Find the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 g of water by 1°C. (a) 4.184 J (b) 1 J (c) 2.09 J (d) 0.239 J
A gas expands from 2.0 L to 5.0 L against a constant pressure of 100 kPa. Convert volumes to m³ and find work done. (a) 400 J (b) 200 J (c) 500 J (d) 300 J
Calculate the work done when a gas is compressed from 6.0 m³ to 2.0 m³ at a pressure of 80 kPa. Use proper sign convention. (a) -320 kJ (b) 320 kJ (c) -640 kJ (d) 640 kJ
Convert 500 calories of heat to joules and then calculate the change in internal energy if 200 J of work is done by the system. (a) 2092 J (b) 1984 J (c) 2280 J (d) 1892 J
A gas is expanded isothermally and reversibly from volume 1 L to 10 L at 298 K. Calculate work done using W = 2.303nRT log(V f /V i ), n=1 mol. (a) 5745 J (b) 5706 J (c) 5900 J (d) 5400 J
Convert 2 kcal of heat into joules and determine the internal energy change if 500 J of work is done on the system. (a) 8386 J (b) 8868 J (c) 8280 J (d) 8184 J
Energy equivalent to one erg, one joule and one calorie are in order: (a) 1 erg > 1 J > 1 cal (b) 1 erg > 1 cal > 1 J (c) 1 cal > 1 J > 1 erg (d) 1 J > 1 cal > 1 erg
Which of the following have same units? (i) Work (ii) Heat (iii) Energy (iv) Entropy (a) (i), (ii) and (iii) (b) (i), (ii) and (iv) (c) (ii), (iii) and (iv) (d) (iii) and (iv)

An ideal gas expands against a constant external pressure of 2.0 atmosphere from 20 litre to 40 litre and absorbs 10 kJ of heat from surrounding. What is the change in internal energy of the system? (Given: 1 atm-litre = 101.3 J) (a) 4052 J (b) 5948 J (c) 14052 J (d) 9940 J

During a process, the internal energy of the system increases by 240 kJ while the system performed 90 kJ of work on its surroundings. How much heat was transferred between the system and the surroundings during this process. In which direction did the heat flow?

The internal energy change when a system goes from state A to B is 40 kJ/mol. If the system goes from A to B by a reversible path and returns to state A by an irreversible path, what would be the net change in internal energy? (a) 40 kJ (b) > 40 kJ (c) < 40 kJ (d) Zero
An ideal gas expands in volume from 10 -3 m³ to 10 -2 m³ at 300 K against a constant pressure of 10 5 Nm -2 . The work done is: (a) 900 kJ (b) -900 kJ (c) 270 kJ (d) -900 J

2 mole of an ideal gas at 27°C expands isothermally and reversibly from a volume of 4 litre to 40 litre. The work done (in kJ) by the gas is: (a) w = -28.72 kJ (b) w = -11.488 kJ (c) w = -5.736 kJ (d) w = -4.988 kJ

A gas absorbs 200 J of heat and expands against the external pressure of 1.5 atm from a volume of 0.5 litre to 1.0 litre. Calculate the change in internal energy. (in J) (a) 122.3 (b) 124.025 (c) 133.4 (d) 121.5

One mole of an ideal gas at 300 K is expanded isothermally from an initial volume of 1 litre to 10 litre. The ΔU for this process is (R = 2 cal K -1 mol -1 ): (a) 163.7 cal (b) 1381.1 cal (c) 9 litre-atm (d) zero
Calculate the maximum work when 24 g of O 2 are expanded isothermally and reversibly from the pressure of 1.6 bar to 1.0 bar at 298 K. (a) 0.67 kJ (b) 1.87 kJ (c) 0.87 kJ (d) 0.1.67 kJ
Which of the following is the correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition? (a) q=0, ΔT<0, w≠0 (b) q=0, ΔT≠0, w=0 (c) q≠0, ΔT=0, w=0 (d) q=0, ΔT=0, w=0
When freezing of a liquid takes place in a system: (a) may have q > 0 or q < 0 depending on the liquid (b) is represented by q > 0 (c) is represented by q < 0 (d) has q = 0

A sample of liquid in a thermally insulated container (a calorimeter) is stirred for 2 hr. by a mechanical linkage to a motor in the surrounding, for this process: (a) w<0, q=0, ΔU=0 (b) w>0, q>0, ΔU>0 (c) w<0, q>0, ΔU=0 (d) w>0, q≈0, ΔU>0

A system undergoes a two-step process: Path 1: Absorbs 150 J of heat and performs 80 J of work. Path 2: Releases 70 J of heat while 40 J of work is done on the system. What is the total change in internal energy (ΔU)?
5 moles of N 2 at 5 atm pressure contained in a 100 L cylinder absorbed 30.26 kJ of heat when it expanded to 200 L at 2 atm. What is the change in internal energy of the gas? (in kJ)
A gas occupies 2 L at NTP. It is provided with 300 J heat so that its volume becomes 2.5 L at 1 atm. Calculate the change in its internal energy.
A gas expands isothermally from 10 dm³ to 20 dm³ at 27°C and work obtained is 4.620 kJ. Calculate the number of moles of the gas. (in mol)
2.5 moles of an ideal gas are expanded isothermally from 12 dm³ to 25 dm³ against a pressure of 3.0 bar. Calculate the work obtained.
Four moles of an ideal gas at 2.5 atm and 27°C are compressed isothermally to half of its volume by an external pressure of 3 atm. Calculate w (in J).

A sample of gas is compressed at a pressure of 0.5 atm from a volume of 400 cm³ to 200 cm³. During the process 8.0 J of heat flows to the surroundings. Calculate the change in the internal energy of the system. (in J)

10 mole of ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly from a pressure of 10 atm to 1 atm at 300 K. What is the largest mass which can be lifted through a height of 100 metre? (a) 31842 kg (b) 58.55 kg (c) 342.58 kg (d) none of these

Calculate the work done in joules when 3 moles of an ideal gas at 27°C expands isothermally and reversibly from 10 atm to 1 atm (1 atm = 1.013×10 5 Nm -2 ). What will be the work done if the expansion is against a constant pressure of 1 atm? (in kJ) (a) +17.23, +6.738 (b) -17.23, -6.738 (c) +17.23, -6.738 (d) -17.23, +6.738

stem: Match Column-I with the appropriate term in Column-II. Column-I: (A) Enthalpy (B) Temperature (C) Free energy (D) Work Column-II: (p) Intrinsic property (q) Path function (r) Function of U, P, V (s) State function (a) (A)→(r), (B)→(p), (C)→(r), (D)→(q) (b) (A)→(s), (B)→(r), (C)→(p), (D)→(q) (c) (A)→(r), (B)→(q), (C)→(p), (D)→(s) (d) (A)→(q), (B)→(s), (C)→(r), (D)→(q)

A 6-litre cylinder contained 280 g of N 2 gas at 27°C. Due to sudden leakage through the hole, all the gas escaped into atmosphere and the cylinder became empty. If the atmospheric pressure is 1.0 atmosphere, calculate the work done by the gas. (in kJ)

[Passage] The state of one mole of an ideal gas changes from state A (pressure 2P, volume V) through four processes and returns to A reversibly, forming a rectangle on the P-V diagram: A(V,2P) → B(2V,2P) → C(2V,P) → D(V,P) → A(V,2P).] Which is the kind of process followed from state A to state B? (a) Isochoric expansion (b) Isobaric expansion (c) Isothermal reversible expansion (d) Isothermal irreversible compression
